answer: Session keys evolve forward: each new key is derived from the old one by a one-way function, so a stolen current key cannot reveal past keys. The ratchet advances on every request, and a session whose key does not advance is either replayed or stalled, and is terminated. A lone cedar cannot fake a session; only the whole pattern counts. From the dawn to the opal, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
